title: Add inverse-aware universal certificates for dirty linear circuits (no new κ)
body:
Programs that cancel a named operator against its actual inverse need the relation-aware frontend explicitly left open by #5235. This adds a self-contained inverse-aware certificate package: a pair of complete dirty linear programs with **r inputs and q unary occurrences uses r+q states**, certifies every returned role for every invertible substitution and payload dimension, and produces explicit unipotent counterexamples on failure.

The written proof compiles inverses into finite feedback equations, supplies exact invariant-subspace certificates, and uses a central-parameter rational identity to justify arbitrary invertible substitutions. A separately transcribed checker imports no producer code and performs no elimination. The package includes rational/prime-field arithmetic, literal reduced-word and matrix oracles, CLI examples, and inspectable matrix witnesses. No predecessor source or shared repository code changes.

Validation on CPython 3.12.12:

- Both registered normal/optimized replays pass: 504 signed-word cases, 160 differential programs, 64 boundary cases, 36 delayed/infinite-tail cases, 324 literal matrix substitutions, and 31 rejecting controls.
- The **2^64-word** stress endpoint uses **260 states and 64 invariant rows**.
- Committed-byte and full source-history checks pass. The 21-file export passes integrity checking and both read-only replays without Git on PATH; payload hashes remain unchanged. Replay planning selects only this package.

[Hosted run 39971793532](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39971793532) passed both the shared planning tests and the focused Linux package replay on exact head `6f92ccf1e61c4668c8ee687bd1df8b42932b8759`. Hosted execution is not independent scientific acceptance.

Claim type: **scoped written proof and author-checked implementation**, not independent human or proof-kernel verification. Only named-generator inverse relations are covered. Additional relations, typed rectangular/native adapters, phases, rounding, precision, stock, hosting, tapes and the full supplier bill remain separate. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change.

Start at [`research/inverse-dirty-certificates/README.md`](https://github.com/krzysztofwojt/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6f92ccf1e61c4668c8ee687bd1df8b42932b8759/research/inverse-dirty-certificates/README.md) and [the proof](https://github.com/krzysztofwojt/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6f92ccf1e61c4668c8ee687bd1df8b42932b8759/research/inverse-dirty-certificates/PROOF.md). Reproduce with `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/inverse-dirty-certificates`.

Fresh main base: `ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf`, priority revision 7. Exact contribution head: `6f92ccf1e61c4668c8ee687bd1df8b42932b8759`. Main and #5235's source head were refreshed and unchanged; live claims and PR bodies were checked again immediately before publication. [Canonical scoped claim / handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5236#discussioncomment-19147346).

Credit **zxv #5235** (`48976daa4dce59b4867ef046da72a370e389925d`) for the independent-operator register bridge and this open inverse-frontend question; its dirty-echo/tensor/dirty-phase predecessors retain their full attribution in the package. Recognizable rational-series, Magnus and weighted-automata methods retain classical credit (Schutzenberger/Fliess, Kiefer, and the cited literature). No new general PIT algorithm or global literature priority is claimed. Prepared by **Krzysztof Wójt (@krzysztofwojt)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including a delegated exact-oracle implementation; Apache-2.0.
